story: I Bought a CO2 Monitor, and It Broke Me
text: > It's not supposed to be sealed, it's just supposed to have draft. It depends on the model. High (>90%) efficiency, condensing furnaces are completely sealed off from the house: they take in air from the outside (via PVC pipe), combust, extract the heat, and exhaust the results (via PVC pipes). * [VIDEO] Older lower efficiency (<85-90%) furnaces suck in air from the house, exhaust into metal pipes (PVC would melt because not as much heat is extracted from the fumes), can be back-drafted and you have to worry about CO. Basically: if the furnace has vents in which you can see a pilot light, it's the older style.

story: Switching to electric stoves can dramatically cut indoor air pollution
text: Technology Connections did a video (because of course he did) on how gas furnaces work. The short of it is that the flame is contained inside of metal tubes and never mixes with indoor air. No exhaust gases can leak into the breathable air. [VIDEO]
